root_cause.text: Memory allocated via sock_kmalloc for crypto context and async request structures was not zero-initialized, causing uninitialized fields such as 'inflight' in af_alg_ctx to contain garbage values that were misinterpreted as true, leading to spurious -EBUSY errors.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description and commit message state: "Because the context is not memset to zero after allocation, the inflight variable has contained garbage values. As a result, af_alg_alloc_areq() has incorrectly returned -EBUSY randomly when the garbage value was interpreted as true." The patch adds `memset(areq, 0, areqlen);` and `memset(ctx, 0, len);` in multiple sites (crypto/af_alg.c, crypto/algif_hash.c, crypto/algif_rng.c) to zero-initialize memory after sock_kmalloc.
